persona.role: retired bookkeeper who volunteers at a hospice

sent_to_model:
Good morning. Our volunteer coordinator, Bridget, has asked me to write this month's piece for the volunteers' blog on the Wensum Vale Hospice website, and she would like it to drum up a few more people for the Thursday tea trolley in the day unit. We have been two short since the summer. Most people who read the blog are local and already fond of the place, but they assume volunteering there must be either harrowing or terribly skilled, and I should like to persuade them otherwise without being sentimental about it. I have jotted down the particulars underneath. Please do not make me sound like a saint. I am nothing of the sort. Please include the time commitment and the induction arrangements.

- Thursday tea trolley, day therapy unit, 1.30 to 4pm. Currently 4 of us on a rota meant for 6. Two left over the summer (one moved to Sheffield to be near grandchildren, one knee op)
- Commitment is one Thursday a fortnight. Bridget does the induction, about two hours, plus a short food hygiene course online which the hospice pays for
- Volunteer open afternoon Tuesday 24 November, 2pm, in the Willow Room. Tea and biscuits, no obligation. Or ring Bridget on the volunteering line
- I started in March 2022, eighteen months after I retired from 41 years of bookkeeping, mostly for a builders' merchant in Dereham
- Day unit sees about 14 to 18 patients on a Thursday. Many come for the art group, the hand massage, or just company. Most go home afterwards
- Mr Hollis, retired signalman, takes two sugars and insists on telling me the 1953 floods each week, slightly differently each time. I have stopped correcting the dates
- My first week I spilled an entire jug of milk over the trolley and a patient called Pat laughed so much she had to be given a tissue. She said it was the best afternoon she'd had in a month
- The bourbon biscuits always go first. We now hide a packet for the late group
- It is not a sad place on a Thursday, mostly. It is noisy and rather jolly. Sad days do happen and the staff look after us when they do
- You do not need any nursing skill. You need to be able to push a trolley, remember who takes what, and listen. 41 years of keeping ledgers straight turns out handy for remembering who takes what
- after retiring had no regular reason to go out most weeks. drifted a bit for 18 months. Thursdays fixed that
- Get at least two people to the open afternoon
- Be honest that some weeks are hard, but not dwell on it

(About me: retired bookkeeper who volunteers at a hospice, 74, Norwich, England. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Recruits volunteers for the Thursday day-unit tea service.
Explains the commitment, induction and lack of a nursing-skill requirement.
Invites readers to the volunteer open afternoon with its date, time and location.
Conveys the usually sociable, cheerful atmosphere of Thursdays and acknowledges difficult weeks without dwelling on them.
